w: Swamishri celebrated Jal Jhilani festival by virtually batting Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Shri Ganeshji. ( See special report )
Through festivals Shriji Maharaj has shown us the path of unbroken communion with God and consolidation of His commands in our lives.
Discourses on God relieve one's fatigue.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
31 Aug 2002, Atladra
35 children from Vaghodiya pilgrimaged by foot to the mandir.
2 Sept 2002, Atladra
Swamishri blessed 20 children who had pilgrimaged 26 km.
4 Sept 2002, Atladra
Over 65 devotees from the village of Zaradka, Alali, Padra and Chansad had pilgrimaged all night in the rain to reach the mandir in the morning.
4 Sept 2002, Nadiad
Swamishri blessed 20 balaks and 5 kishores for having pilgrimaged 12 km.

On 17 September 2002, the festival of Jal Jhilani was celebrated in Sarangpur at the river Utavali (Shighra Ganga) in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. A beautiful lotus-shaped sinhasan had been placed in the middle of the river. There, after the traditional Vedic pujan rituals, Swamishri blessed the assembly seated on the banks. Then, Swamishri bathed the murti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj with water from the holy rivers of Ganga, Yamuna, Mansarovar and Utavali.

Then Swamishri, with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Ganapatiji, sat in a boat and after sailing in the river returned to shore where the first of the five artis was traditionally performed. Then they made another round in the river, before returning to shore for the second arti. In this way, five artis were performed.
The sadhus and many of the devotees had observed a waterless fast, as per the traditional custom and the wishes of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj.

After his morning routine of darshan, puja and breakfast, Swamishri had a series of meetings to attend. Since the meetings could last till noon, Swamishri asked whether it would do if he did not attend the morning assembly. A sadhu organizing the assembly program sent a message that it would be alright if he could not come.

Swamishri could have sent word that he would not come, but instead, he took permission from the organizer. Swamishri's humility and discipline in his working method is inspiring and worthy of emulation.

Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav Despite ill health, Swamishri had come specially for the inauguration of this new BAPS mandir. Swamishri performed the traditional Vedic murti-pratishtha ceremony of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha-Krishna Dev and the Guru Parampara. Then blessing the assembly Swamishri said, “The aim of human life is liberation. That is why, to guide man, Bhagwan Purushottam Narayan incarnated on this earth with His abode (ideal devotee – Gunatitanand Swami). With the blessings of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, Satsang has grown in India and abroad. “Gardens give fragrance to all, water quenches thirst, trees give shade, similarly, God and His Sadhu work to benefit others. By their darshan, done knowingly or unknowingly, one attains peace – just as one becomes immortal if one drinks nectar even unknowingly.”
In the evening assembly, the Indian High Commissioner, Lal Mavana, was present.

In the evening assembly youths and children presented a cultural programme themed ‘Colouring Mumbai’. A drama on a parable by Yogiji Maharaj ‘Titodi’s Eggs’ was enacted. It reflected the message of samp, suhrudbhav and ekta. Thereafter a cultural dance was performed by children. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “How many people would be required to colour the whole of Mumbai (with values)? If you persevere with faith and patience then it can be done. Nothing is impossible. Pebble by pebble you can build a wall. If you endeavour little by little with faith, then a great work can be accomplished. When you study regularly you gradually attain a degree. You can become a doctor, scientist or an engineer…”

At 11.47 am Swamishri and his entourage of sadhus and devotees departed by flight from Chino Hills (LA) and landed at La Guardia airport at 7.45 pm (4.45 pm LA time). At 8.00 pm Swamishri arrived at the BAPS Swaminarayan hari mandir in Flushing, New York.

Kirtan Patel, a satsangi kishore, asked Swamishri, “Next year I’ll be going to college. What should I be careful about?” Swamishri replied, “Study properly in college, and be firm about satsang. Take care of your niyams. Be careful you do not fall into bad company and do not become friends with mischievous boys. Also be careful that you do not lapse in remaining vegetarian. In short, stay with good boys, remain vegetarian, pay attention to your studies and watch only good programmes on TV.” Then Kirtan requested “Give me one niyam.” Swamishri replied, “Inspire one boy to become a satsangi every year. This will also strengthen your own faith. To achieve this read our satsang books regularly.” Kirtan further asked, “Maharaj has spoken about the glory of the Satpurush in many Vachanamruts. How can one understand his true glory?” Swamishri answered, “Through love for the Satpurush the soul becomes attached to him. Then whatever he says or instructs one believes it to be right. Through love one comes closer to him, trusts him and becomes deeply attached to him.”

Out of many devotees who had performed austerities, Jayesh Desai observed a 100-hour waterless fast. Shailya, a child, observed liquid fasts for 30 days and Shyam fasted on liquid for three weeks. Three female youths, nine female teenagers and six women devotees observed liquid fasts and two women observed dharna-parna vrat.
6 September 2007, San Jose
Since 2005, 110 women devotees have been observing chain-fasts for Swamishri’s good health.
Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the Pramukh Swami Mandapam. Here, the couples getting married and engaged and their families had taken their places. On this occasion, Swamishri spoke words of affection:

"Marriage is a sacred ceremony. It is not a bargain of looks and qualities. This is exactly where problems arise. People look at outward looks but do not look at qualities. Marriage is a bond tied with the delicate silk thread of loyalty and love. The sacred bond of marriage is a vow to stand by each other at every moment of life, in happiness or sorrow, in success or failure. Marriage is the resolve made by two people to stay with each other for life. Marriage is a vow to be loyal to each other. The man looks for the best wife and the woman looks for the best husband. But it should not be like that. Instead, it should be done in this way: 'I will be the best husband and I will be the best wife.' Then it will last right to the end."

The clarity about married life that even people bound in marriage for 50 or 60 years may not have flowed from every single sentence of Swamishri, who is steadfast in brahmacharya. This is exactly the special quality of our gurus: they can give precise guidance on any subject.

Sureshbhai had come from Tampa for Mahant Swami Maharaj's darshan. His daughter had passed away just twelve days earlier because of pneumonia. But the family had shown great strength and understanding. They had not grieved at all. But today the family, who had come here, had a question asked: "Our daughter's soul is in Akshardham, isn't it? If you say it with your own lips, everyone will be convinced."
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "We see it directly."
It was such a sharp statement that even the expression "unobstructed vision" falls short for Swamishri.

At mealtime, Mahant Swami Maharaj put a mouthful of food in his mouth and, even while chewing, began to meet the devotees with folded hands through his glance. He did the same with the second mouthful too.
The attendant sadhu said, "Swami takes one mouthful and folds his hands... he keeps folding his hands, so these are personal meetings going on. He meets each one with his eyes. They feel satisfied."
Swamishri said in a voice full of feeling, "Whether they feel satisfied or not, we certainly do."
Swamishri must surely have been speaking of the satisfaction of faithfully carrying out the responsibility his guru had entrusted to him!
Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the launch ceremony of the text "Swaminarayan Siddhanta Sudha," being held in the garden behind the sadhus' ashram.

Pujya Swami Shri Paramacharyaji, who was present on this occasion, gave a beautiful analysis of the role of the guru in philosophical study on this occasion of "Akshar Purushottam Darshan," and at the end said, "Now we honour Pramukh Swami Maharaj, whom I met on this very stage when he last came here. And today here I am also meeting his wonderful form, Mahant Swamiji Maharaj."
He too had become convinced that Pramukh Swami Maharaj is manifest today through Mahant Swami Maharaj.

As the programme went on, Shri Sthaneshwarji Timalsina, a renowned Sanskrit scholar from San Diego State University, in a talk for the occasion, described his experience of first meeting Mahant Swami Maharaj:

"When I went to LA to receive this Swaminarayan Siddhanta Sudha text, I had the darshan of Mahant Swamiji Maharaj. He asked me, 'Why did you leave Nepal? What compelled you?' I said, 'At that time there was a Maoist movement there. The Maoists were targeting Sanskrit and those who teach Sanskrit. One day, while I was teaching in college, they threw stones. I lost consciousness. I was admitted to hospital. When I woke up, I found that my head had been broken, but even more than that, my heart had been broken.

We have enemies, but we are not weak either. We will not let any harm come to Indian culture, because we have such sadhus to guide us. So no one can measure our strength. No one has any idea of our strength, because we are connected with truth and non violence.
Then Swami touched my head and asked, 'Where were you hurt?' And two or three times he said, 'Bhagwan protected you.'

This experience filled my eyes with tears. I took my leave. Seeing the tears in my eyes, my student, who was driving the car, asked, 'What happened?' Then I told him, 'Three months ago my mother passed away, and 45 days after her my guruji, who had taught me everything, also passed away. But today, when Swamishri touched my head, I felt that my mother was touching me. My guruji was touching me once again.' I was overwhelmed by that feeling, and my eyes and heart were filled.
The shade of a father, the love of a mother,
I found a friend and brother, who stood by me as my support.
O Guru! In difficulties you lifted me up in your arms,
And so you have made me forever indebted to you."
Everyone who comes into contact with Swamishri has such an experience.
